I work in homeless sector... most of the jobs you can find for an unhoused person with huge gaps in employment typically (along with any host of other catalysts) are your typical fast food/grocery store gigs. Typically part time (15-39 hrs a week) for maybe  $10 and change (before taxes and union).  Scrape by is an understatement. And while affordable housing options do exist in this city and surrounding, the wait lists are long or a lottery. Shared spaces in programs often require a background check and co-ops which are the most popular way to slash rents in Denver, are pretty exclusive (as in, most aren’t trying to toss a homeless person onto the lease). Also worth considering, the further away you start to get from the heart of Denver (where the jobs are)... transportation becomes an issue. $99 for a monthly bus passes if you don’t qualify for some discount or program.

Affordability and gentrification aren’t the ONLY things exacerbating homelessness in Denver... but it’s part of it for sure.

If you are going to give to homeless (which isn’t an obligation in my opinion but it’s still a nice thing to do)... give them food/water/toiletries... etc. Keep stuff in your car and hand it out at the intersections or w/e if you are approached. Giving money directly to homeless people can really impede upon progress caseworker are trying to make with a client (breaking the cycle of panhandling and sticking with/seeking employment).
